name: Cognitive Reframing
description: Identifying and challenging distorted thought patterns by replacing negative automatic thoughts with balanced, realistic ones.
keywords: negative thoughts reframing cognitive distortion thinking patterns challenge evidence balanced

name: Behavioral Activation
description: Scheduling pleasurable and meaningful activities to break the cycle of depression-inactivity-depression. Helps restore a sense of accomplishment and pleasure.
steps: Identify activities that bring pleasure or mastery
keywords: depression activity schedule pleasure accomplishment motivation routine

name: Thought Record (ABC Model)
description: Structured journaling technique using the Activating event - Beliefs - Consequences model to trace emotional responses back to core beliefs.
keywords: journaling beliefs thoughts consequences ABC model dispute evidence rational

name: Decatastrophizing
description: A technique to challenge catastrophic thinking by examining actual probabilities and coping ability if the feared outcome occurs.
steps: Ask: What is the actual probability?
Ask: What is the worst realistic outcome?
Ask: Could I cope with that?
keywords: catastrophe worst case probability realistic thinking cope disaster anxiety panic

name: Socratic Questioning
description: Guided discovery technique using gentle questioning to help clients examine and revise unhelpful beliefs.
steps: Ask: What evidence supports this thought?
Ask: Is there another way to look at this?
Ask: What would you tell a friend in this situation?
Ask: What is the effect of believing this?
keywords: questions evidence perspective self-compassion friend advice balanced thinking

name: Graded Exposure
description: Systematic desensitization to feared situations through gradual, controlled exposure starting from least to most anxiety-provoking.
steps: Stay in situation until anxiety reduces by 50%
keywords: exposure fear hierarchy avoidance anxiety phobia gradual practice

name: Mindfulness Meditation
description: Non-judgmental present-moment awareness practice that reduces rumination and increases psychological flexibility.
steps: Notice when mind wanders without judgment
keywords: mindfulness meditation breath present moment non-judgmental awareness calm focus

name: Values Clarification (ACT)
description: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy technique to identify what truly matters to the person and guide committed action aligned with values.
steps: List important life domains (family, work, health, relationships)
Rate current satisfaction in each domain
Identify core values in each domain
keywords: values purpose meaning ACT acceptance committed action life domains

name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
description: Systematic tensing and releasing of muscle groups to reduce physical tension associated with anxiety and stress.
steps: Tense each muscle group for 5-7 seconds
keywords: muscle relaxation tension release body stress anxiety physical somatic

name: Cognitive Defusion (ACT)
description: Creating distance from unhelpful thoughts by observing them as mental events rather than facts or commands.
steps: Notice the thought (e.g., I am a failure)
Label it: My mind is having the thought that...
Visualize thoughts as clouds passing by
Thank your mind for the thought
keywords: defusion thoughts observer self ACT distance metaphor clouds passing

name: Problem-Solving Therapy
description: Structured approach to identify problems, generate solutions, evaluate options, and implement the best choice.
steps: Define the problem clearly and specifically
Brainstorm all possible solutions without judgment
Evaluate pros and cons of each
Choose and implement the best solution
Evaluate outcome and adjust if needed
keywords: problem solving steps brainstorm options decision making action plan

name: Self-Compassion Break (Neff)
description: Three-component mindfulness practice: mindfulness (acknowledging pain), common humanity (we all suffer), and self-kindness (treating yourself as a friend).
steps: Acknowledge: This is a moment of suffering
Remind yourself: Suffering is part of life
Place hand on heart and say: May I be kind to myself
Ask: What do I need right now?
Give yourself what you would give a good friend
keywords: self compassion kindness suffering humanity friend inner critic gentle
